boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places with documented uses for studying, meeting, recreation, and downtime, selected from current Hampden-Sydney sources.

cards.title: Settle In at Brown Student Center
cards.subtitle: Lounge, games, student services, and pond-side outdoor space
cards.notes: Use the communal areas for a club meetup or study break, then step onto the terrace overlooking Chalgrove Pond for fresh air.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose gathering place combining informal recreation, student offices, food service, and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney identifies Brown Student Center as a campus-life hub with student organization space, pool and ping-pong tables, lounges, and outdoor communal areas overlooking Chalgrove Pond.
cards.access_notes: Campus facilities are privately owned; students should follow posted building access rules and current operating schedules.

cards.title: Claim a Group Room at Bortz
cards.subtitle: Library study space with reservable-room potential and academic support nearby
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from a shared table, and check the library’s current room and building policies before gathering your group.
cards.short_summary: The campus library supports collaborative study and places academic and computing help in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s fact book reports 11 group-study rooms at Bortz Library, while the current campus map places the Office of Academic Success and Fuqua Computing Center in the same building.
cards.access_notes: Library access and room availability may vary by academic calendar; consult current library notices before visiting.

cards.title: Handle the Technical Part at Fuqua
cards.subtitle: Ground-floor computer, scanning, and printing facilities inside Bortz Library
cards.notes: Come here when an assignment needs a campus computer, scan, or print job; confirm current service access before relying on a deadline visit.
cards.short_summary: A practical technology stop for finishing the production side of coursework inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney states that the John B. Fuqua Computing Center is on Bortz Library’s ground level and contains a computer lab plus scanning and printing facilities.
cards.access_notes: Use is governed by College and library access policies; verify current lab availability and printing requirements.

cards.title: Meet Around the Technology Commons
cards.subtitle: A named academic and student-service destination on the campus map
cards.notes: Use the commons as a clearly identifiable meetup point for technology-centered work, then confirm any room-specific rules on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed campus workspace suited to coordinating technology-dependent academic tasks.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney’s interactive campus map lists Fuqua Technology Commons under both Academic Facilities and Student Services.
cards.access_notes: The map confirms the destination but not public access or hours; follow current campus and building restrictions.

cards.title: Workshop an Argument at Pannill
cards.subtitle: The physical center of Hampden-Sydney’s rhetoric program
cards.notes: Bring a draft or presentation idea and use the center as your destination for rhetoric-focused practice, feedback, and revision planning.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated academic setting for sharpening writing and speaking work with others.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney says the Pannill Center places its central rhetoric program in the physical center of campus and focuses on clear writing and speaking.
cards.access_notes: Academic services and rooms may require an appointment or College affiliation; check current program guidance.

cards.title: Take the Conversation to Wright Point
cards.subtitle: A named lakeside destination near the center of campus life
cards.notes: Choose Wright Point for a daylight conversation or outdoor reset, and respect weather conditions, shoreline boundaries, and campus rules.
cards.short_summary: A clearly mapped lakeside point that gives small groups an outdoor alternative to indoor common rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney’s interactive map lists Wright Point at Chalgrove Lake as a named sports-and-recreation location, and the College describes student space overlooking the lake.
cards.access_notes: Visit during safe daylight and suitable weather; campus property is private and posted restrictions apply.

cards.title: Walk a Loop on Wilson Trail
cards.subtitle: A campus hiking route identified as an accessible recreation amenity
cards.notes: Use the trail for a walking meeting or study reset; take water, wear suitable shoes, and turn back if weather or trail conditions deteriorate.
cards.short_summary: A named campus route where students can pair light outdoor activity with an unhurried conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney names Wilson Hiking Trail among its readily accessible student recreation amenities, and the interactive map lists Wilson Trail as a recreation location.
cards.source_title: What to Do at Hampden-Sydney College
cards.access_notes: Use only during suitable conditions and comply with campus notices, closures, and private-property restrictions.

cards.title: Move the Meetup to TigeRec
cards.subtitle: Individual workouts and group fitness for the College community
cards.notes: Coordinate a workout or class with friends, but check the current facility notice first because closures and schedules can change.
cards.short_summary: A shared recreation facility for individual exercise and organized group fitness.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney says the TigeRec Fitness Center supports individual workouts and group fitness classes and permits current students, faculty, staff, alumni, and members.
cards.access_notes: The current TigeRec page says the fitness center and basketball courts are closed until further notice; verify status before going.

cards.title: Share a Lane at Leggett Pool
cards.subtitle: Recreational and lap swimming for the Hampden-Sydney community
cards.notes: Plan a lap-swim session during a posted open block, enter through the patio doors, and check in with pool staff as directed.
cards.short_summary: A community pool with documented recreational use and specific check-in instructions.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney describes Leggett Pool as open to its community for recreational use and lap swimming and publishes current access instructions and schedules.
cards.access_notes: Follow the current pool schedule, use the patio-side entrance, and check in with pool staff; no day passes or new memberships are currently offered.

cards.title: Play Nine at Tadpole Holes
cards.subtitle: A nine-hole campus course beginning and ending near Kirk Athletic Center
cards.notes: Meet outside Kirk Athletic Center for a nine-hole round, keep clear of other users, and account for water and wooded fairway hazards.
cards.short_summary: A mapped recreational course that gives a group a defined outdoor activity and meeting point.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney states that its disc golf course has nine par-3 holes across three-quarters of a mile, begins and ends outside Kirk Athletic Center, and is open to area community members.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to weather, campus rules, and any posted course restrictions; bring or confirm access to appropriate equipment.
